run.question: Use the custom-crd runbook and check why custom CRD whale-watcher resources are not being reconciled by the operator in namespace app-96

report.summary: The requested custom-crd runbook is not among this target's approved runbooks (the list contains only skill_id 'service-troubleshooting', which is about service connectivity and does not match this problem), so no runbook steps were executed. What the cluster evidence does show: CRD whalewatchers.ocean.io (group ocean.io, kind WhaleWatcher, Namespaced, v1 served/storage) is installed and Established, and the only reconciler candidate cluster-wide is Deployment app-96/whale-operator, whose pod is Running and Ready with 0 restarts. The one object-level fault found in the reconcile path is RBAC: ClusterRole whale-operator, bound to ServiceAccount app-96/whale-operator by ClusterRoleBinding whale-operator, contains a single rule granting only get, list and watch on ocean.io/whalewatchers; it grants no update/patch, and the v1 CRD enables no status subresource even though the schema declares status.phase, status.observationCount and status.lastSeen. So the operator can read the whale-watcher resources but has no permission to write reconcile results back to them — the strongest supported explanation for resources appearing unreconciled — although no 403 was observed directly. A second, competing explanation is timing: namespace app-96, the Deployment, its ReplicaSet and its Pod were all created at 2026-11-22T09:29:48Z, about 39 s before my first query, so for almost all of the authorized window no operator process existed in app-96 and only a startup interval had elapsed at query time. The custom resources themselves could not be read with the tools available in this Run, the operator's code Secret could not be read, its container produced no log lines in either log read, and Prometheus returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so neither a 403 nor a stuck watch could be confirmed.

claims.text: The custom resource definition whalewatchers.ocean.io exists (group ocean.io, kind WhaleWatcher, plural whalewatchers, Namespaced, version v1 served and storage) with conditions NamesAccepted=True and Established=True, so the CRD itself is not the reason for missing reconciliation.

The whalewatchers.ocean.io v1 schema declares a status object with fields lastSeen, observationCount and phase, and its version entry contains no subresources setting, i.e. no status subresource is enabled, so status can only be written by update/patch on the whalewatchers resource itself.
ClusterRoleBinding whale-operator binds ServiceAccount whale-operator in namespace app-96 to ClusterRole whale-operator (cluster-scoped).

ClusterRole whale-operator contains exactly one rule: apiGroups ["ocean.io"], resources ["whalewatchers"], verbs ["get","list","watch"]. It grants no update, patch, create or delete verb and no whalewatchers/status resource, so the operator's identity can read whale-watcher resources but cannot write to them.

Deployment whale-operator in namespace app-96 was created 2026-11-22T09:29:48Z with generation 1 and kubectl last-applied annotation, spec.replicas 1, readyReplicas 1 and availableReplicas 1, conditions Available=True (MinimumReplicasAvailable) and Progressing=True (NewReplicaSetAvailable); its container runs command ["python","/app/operator.py"] on image python:3.9-slim with serviceAccountName whale-operator and mounts Secret whale-operator at /app, with env OPERATOR_NAMESPACE from fieldRef metadata.namespace.

Pod whale-operator-5f695b7c66-tbr4q was created 2026-11-22T09:29:48Z, its operator container started at 2026-11-22T09:29:50Z and is running and ready, with restartCount 0 and an empty lastState, and its only owner is ReplicaSet whale-operator-5f695b7c66.
ReplicaSet whale-operator-5f695b7c66 in namespace app-96 was created 2026-11-22T09:29:48Z, is owned by Deployment whale-operator and reports 1 replica with 1 ready.

Namespace app-96 was created 2026-11-22T09:29:48Z and is Active, i.e. the namespace holding the whale-watcher resources and the operator was itself about 39 seconds old when the cluster objects were read.

The event list for the authorized window across all namespaces contains 7 events, none of whose involvedObject.kind is WhaleWatcher; the app-96 entries are Normal events only (ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate, Deployment ScalingReplicaSet "Scaled up replica set whale-operator-5f695b7c66 from 0 to 1", and Pod Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started) all at 09:29:48-09:29:50Z.

Across all 25 Deployments in the cluster, whale-operator in app-96 (created 2026-11-22T09:29:48Z) is the only Deployment whose name contains "whale"; no other workload in another namespace appears as an alternative reconciler for WhaleWatcher resources.

The operator's own pod state does not show a crash loop, OOM kill or eviction: container operator is running and ready, restartCount 0, lastState empty, and Deployment whale-operator reports Available=True with 1 ready replica, so the operator failure is not explained by a damaged or restarted pod.

Rejected: the CRD being absent, unserved or not established. whalewatchers.ocean.io is present with Established=True and NamesAccepted=True, so missing reconciliation is not caused by the CRD registration.

Primary hypothesis: reconciliation results cannot be persisted because the operator's identity is read-only. ClusterRole whale-operator grants only get/list/watch on ocean.io/whalewatchers, and because the v1 CRD enables no status subresource, writing status.phase/observationCount/lastSeen requires update or patch on whalewatchers; each such write would be rejected with 403 Forbidden, leaving the custom resources unchanged so they appear unreconciled. This mechanism is inferred from the role verbs and CRD schema; a 403 itself was not observed (no log lines, no audit trail).

Alternative hypothesis: the reported non-reconciliation reflects a freshly created stack rather than a stuck controller. Namespace app-96, Deployment whale-operator, its ReplicaSet and its Pod were all created at 2026-11-22T09:29:48-09:29:50Z, only seconds before the state was read, and the container had produced no log output yet; a reconcile loop may simply not have completed a first cycle at the time of observation.

Verify the mechanism before changing anything: read the WhaleWatcher objects in app-96 (spec/status, e.g. kubectl get whalewatchers -n app-96 -o yaml) and the whale-operator container logs after the pod has run for several minutes, looking for 403 Forbidden responses on update/patch of whalewatchers. If those appear, extend ClusterRole whale-operator with update/patch on ocean.io/whalewatchers (and consider enabling a status subresource plus whalewatchers/status verbs) instead of widening it to unrelated resources.

Obtain and run the actually requested custom-crd runbook: this target's approved runbook list contains only skill_id 'service-troubleshooting' (service connectivity), which does not match CRD reconciliation, so its steps were deliberately not applied here.

gaps: The requested custom-crd runbook is not in the approved runbook list (only 'service-troubleshooting' is listed), so no custom-CRD runbook steps could be carried out or reported.

No tool in this Run can read ocean.io/whalewatchers custom resources (the Kubernetes tools accept only the fixed kind list, which excludes custom resources), so the WhaleWatcher objects' existence, spec, status.phase/observationCount/lastSeen, and generation vs observed state could not be observed at all.

Secret whale-operator (mounted at /app, holding the operator code operator.py) cannot be read, so what the operator watches and whether it attempts status writes or other writes (e.g. events, jobs) is unknown; the RBAC mechanism is therefore inferred, not observed.

Both log reads of pod whale-operator-5f695b7c66-tbr4q (default window 2026-11-22T08:30:27Z-09:30:27Z with limit 200, and an explicit 2026-11-22T09:29:40Z-09:30:27Z window with limit 500) returned zero lines and status no_data, so no operator error text (such as a 403) is available.
Prometheus was unreachable in this Run: get_metric_names returned status error / SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE twice, so no metric could confirm or refute reconciliation activity or the operator's health.

The change_history integration is not available, so who or what created namespace app-96 and Deployment whale-operator at 2026-11-22T09:29:48Z, and whether an earlier operator existed and was removed, is unknown.

Queries for RoleBindings and Roles in namespace app-96 returned nothing (status no_data), which cannot be cited as proof that no namespaced RBAC grant exists; only the ClusterRole/ClusterRoleBinding picture is established.
Whether the custom resources predate the operator (i.e. were created before 09:29:48Z) is unknown, so the claim that they were unreconciled for long cannot be dated.
next_steps: Read the WhaleWatcher resources in app-96 directly (spec, metadata.generation, status) to establish which of them are unreconciled and since when.
After the operator has been running for several minutes, collect its container logs and look for watch/reconcile output and for 403 Forbidden errors on update/patch of ocean.io/whalewatchers.

If 403s are confirmed, add update and patch (and, if a status subresource is enabled, whalewatchers/status update/patch) to ClusterRole whale-operator for apiGroups ocean.io, resources whalewatchers, then re-check that status.phase/observationCount/lastSeen start changing.

If no 403 appears, treat the current state as a fresh-deployment startup and re-evaluate after the operator has had a full reconcile cycle; also confirm from the operator code in Secret whale-operator which resources it needs to write (events, jobs, pods) and that those verbs are granted.
Provide the custom-crd runbook for this target if it is expected to exist, since only 'service-troubleshooting' is currently approved.
